title: SendLit vs Listmonk, Mautic, beehiiv & More
description: Compare SendLit with beehiiv, Kit, Loops, Listmonk, Mautic and MailCheap: pricing, who sends your email, sequences, transactional email and API code.

settings.content:
Compare

SendLit vs the Alternatives

Hosted SendLit at app.sendlit.app gives you newsletters, sequences and transactional email, priced by the emails you send and never by the size of your list. Start free with 3,000 emails a month, then $10, $29 or $99. Everything in the app is in the REST API, and the MCP server lets your AI agents do everything you do day to day. Below, we compare it with six popular options at real list sizes. Where we could not confirm something, we say so.

SendLit vs beehiiv

beehiiv is a hosted newsletter platform with a website builder, growth tools and monetization built in. It prices by subscriber, so the bill climbs with your list. Hosted SendLit prices by the emails you send, with unlimited contacts, and everything in the app is in the REST API, with an MCP server for everything you do day to day.

Questions

Why does the cost gap grow with my list?

beehiiv prices by subscriber count: Lite is $139 a month at 10,000 subscribers and $469 at 100,000, billed monthly. Hosted SendLit prices by emails sent, with unlimited contacts, so 100,000 subscribers emailed weekly is Business at $99 plus about $40–$64 of Amazon SES.

What do I need to get started?

A free SendLit account and a sending account you connect, such as Amazon SES, Postmark or any SMTP server. If you use Amazon SES, AWS reviews your account before it lets you send to everyone.

Can I import my beehiiv list?

Yes. Import beehiiv’s CSV export into SendLit; the subscription tier becomes a tag.

Does SendLit build a newsletter website?

No. SendLit sends email. beehiiv also hosts your newsletter’s website and monetization tools.

Hosted SendLit prices by emails sent, adds transactional email and a team per customer, and puts everything in the app in its REST API, with an MCP server for day-to-day work.

Questions

Is Loops free?

Loops has a free plan with up to 4,000 sends every 30 days to your first 1,000 contacts, and a “Powered by Loops” footer. Paid plans start at $49 a month for up to 5,000 subscribed contacts, with unlimited sends.

Which costs less as I grow?

At 10,000 contacts emailed weekly, Loops is $99 a month and SendLit Pro plus Amazon SES is about $33–$35. At 100,000, Loops is $399 and SendLit Business plus SES is about $139–$163.

Does Loops send the email for me?

Yes. Loops sends from its own infrastructure; you add a few DNS records. SendLit sends through the provider you connect, such as Amazon SES or Postmark, so the sending account and its reputation are yours.

Can I import from Loops?

Yes. Export your contacts from Loops as CSV and import them into SendLit with column mapping.

SendLit vs Listmonk

Listmonk is a fast, self-hosted newsletter and mailing list manager: one Go binary and PostgreSQL, around since 2018. It is excellent at broadcasting to big lists, but you run the server, and there are no autoresponders. Hosted SendLit is the same idea, an open-source core with no per-subscriber fee, without running a server, and it adds sequences, transactional email and a team per customer.

Questions

Why pay for SendLit instead of self-hosting Listmonk?

You don’t run a server, so there is nothing for you to size, upgrade or keep online. You also get multi-step sequences, a transactional email API, a team per customer, and an MCP server, which Listmonk doesn’t have. Contacts are unlimited on every SendLit plan, so a big list doesn’t raise your bill.

Is Listmonk faster at big sends?

Listmonk is built for raw throughput: its site describes a 7M+ email campaign on a fraction of one CPU core with a 57 MB memory peak. SendLit queues sends for you and lets you set a per-provider send rate and a warm-up limit.

Can I bring my Listmonk subscribers?

Yes. Export them as CSV and import the file into SendLit, mapping columns as you go.

SendLit vs Mautic

Mautic is a full open-source marketing automation suite: contacts, a website tracking script, points, stages, forms, landing pages and campaign builders, on PHP and MySQL. If you want all of that, it is a strong choice, but it is a lot to run. Hosted SendLit gives you an open-source core focused on newsletters, sequences and product email, without running a server, and everything in the app is in its REST API, with an MCP server for day-to-day work.

Questions

Which is easier to run?

Hosted SendLit: there is nothing to run. Sign up, connect your sending account and send. Mautic needs PHP 8.2, MySQL or MariaDB and cron jobs for segments, campaigns and sending, and you keep it upgraded and backed up.

Does SendLit track website visitors like Mautic?

No. Mautic’s tracking script, points and stages are built for scoring anonymous and known visitors. SendLit tracks email delivery, opens and clicks, and leaves web analytics to other tools.

Can I move from Mautic?

Yes. Export your contacts as CSV and import them into SendLit with column mapping.

SendLit vs MailCheap

MailCheap, by Marc Lou, is a newsletter app: write an issue, send it to your list, publish it on the web. It is open source, priced per email, and everything in the app is in its REST API, with an MCP server for day-to-day work. MailCheap Cloud includes sending; it has a welcome email, not multi-step sequences. Hosted SendLit is also open source and per email, without running a server, and adds sequences, transactional email, a team per customer and the provider of your choice.
